overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance data reveals that extreme cosmic scenarios, extreme planetary environments, and hypothetical 'What If' space questions drive the highest velocity of views and engagement (likes-per-view) over the recent 7-day window. Videos such as 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year', 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?', and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' outperform standard static facts by combining counterintuitive science with high-stakes hypothetical survival hooks.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on surreal planetary conditions or survival questions (e.g., IYuce8vaU3Y with 1024 views/38 likes, A9Qa-RmuOr0 with 968 views/21 likes) generated significantly higher engagement velocity than general historical or psychological facts.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on high-concept space and planetary physics 'What If' scenarios that feature extreme, visually compelling physical conditions.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring bizarre material interactions on distant celestial bodies—such as liquid diamond, extreme darkness (TrES-2b), or unusual planetary timing—prompt strong curiosity loops.
winning_patterns.action: Structure hook openings around paradoxes or impossible-sounding physical states in outer space.

weak_patterns.evidence: Shorts covering minor psychological tricks or common biological notes (e.g., 2fqaGqfsR4A, Jc04LVKNd2s) stagnated heavily with single-digit or low double-digit views.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize minor psychological trivia unless paired with a high-stakes, cinematic micro-story or intense mystery.

weak_patterns.pattern: Static Declarative Space Facts Without Stakes
weak_patterns.evidence: Simple declarative statements about space without a compelling narrative or experiential hook (e.g., vFXHTmYITp4) failed to capture audience attention.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid passive phrasing; frame every space fact as an active, urgent mystery or experiential question.
